newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie bounces as bulls dare to hope.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie bounces as bulls dare to hope.

text.p: *AUD starts at one-week high after short squeeze on break of $0.7380 reached $0.7440/50 resistance band offshore
*Analysts see scope for more gains to $0.7475/80 on pure chart view, but all depends on whether RBA cuts rates this week
*Bulls have dared to hope bank will not ease after all but majority feel it probable if CPI and wages data are benign
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar was hovering at US$0.7420/25 having climbed from US$0.7390/95 late here Friday.

That was its best start since July 10, the day when a lacklustre June employment report saw the market fully price in another rate cut and the dollar crack key US$0.7410 support for the first time this downtrend.

The 90-day bank bill future touched a contract high of 94.99 afterwards, implying a rate of 5.01 percent against the 5.50 percent cash rate. The market had begun to have second thoughts since, partly because of the very weakness of the dollar, but the contract was still at 94.86 refecting the balance of risks.

A$ bulls had dared to hope they might escape a cut after former RBA governor Bernie Fraser's comment Friday that the authorities had missed an opportunity to slip in a fifth easing. However, most analysts continued to believe the economy was soft enough to warrant an easing and inflation low enough to justify one.

The latter point should be driven home when consumer price data for the June quarter are released on Wednesday. Median forecasts have been drifting down for the last month and now favour an actual fall of 0.1 percent in the CPI measure which would take annual growth to just 0.5 percent from 1.3 percent.

Underlying inflation, which the RBA explicitly targets, is seen rising 0.4 percent taking annual growth to 1.7 percent from 2.1 percent. That would be under the bank's 2-3 percent target band and lowest reading since the series began back in 1971.

Given such an impressive result, and assuming wages data on Thursday did not prove much stronger than expected, analysts reckoned a cut would be odds-on either for Friday or for August 6, the day after the next RBA board meeting.
The A$ would be vulnerable while the uncertainty lasted, particularly as dealers were no longer sure how much risk of a rate cut was actually priced in. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
